correctness.rationale: With four exact uniform pairwise-independent p-values, the five bin probabilities are α/4 for each of the first four bins and 1−α for the fifth. Simes rejection is exactly N1≥1 or N1+N2≥2 or N1+N2+N3≥3 or N5=0. The explicit quadratic polynomial B(N) in RESULT.md majorizes this indicator on all 70 weak five-part compositions of four. Pairwise moments E[Nj(Nj−1)]=12pj² and E[NjNk]=12pjpk yield E[B]=α+13α²/16. All 13 support-state weights of the explicit exchangeable extremizer are nonnegative for 0≤α≤2/5, sum to 1, and match all five first moments and all fifteen same/different bin factorial moments. On each support state B=indicator; independent exact symbolic reimplementation verified every inequality, polynomial moment, normalization, and objective, including 333/6400 at α=1/20. Uniform conditional sampling inside bins makes all P_i exactly continuous Uniform[0,1] and every coordinate pair independent. It does not establish behavior for α>2/5.

originality.rationale: The previously published three-variable pairwise-independent Simes envelope has leading α+4α²/9, but its 20-state moment problem does not imply the four-variable 70-state extremum. The original pairwise-independent probability-bound literature treats union and sum-tail events, not this nested 1-of-4/2-of-4/3-of-4/4-of-4 Simes region. Hommel 1983 full eight-page primary text, retrieved through authorized access after unsuccessful OA/preprint search, concerns sharp arbitrary-dependence bounds for adjusted overall tests; it does not impose pairwise independent uniform marginals or yield coefficient 13/16. No stronger prior coverage found.
residual_risks: The 1983 Hommel full text was independently read via authorized access; the exact 1979 dissertation referenced for sharpness was not obtained. An older finite moment LP under different terminology could still contain the numerical 13/16 coefficient.
The 13-state extremizer weights become negative beyond α=2/5; sharpness or formula above that boundary is not asserted.
Formal proof is exact symbolic moment verification plus pointwise 70-state inequality; no exhaustive search of all historical joint-law optimization papers was possible.
